english_verification.review_scope: Checked H81's English name, ruler and dynasty, national-idea names/text/effects, the H81 mission-group Tag gate, a representative colonization/institution mission gate, a vampire/frenzy mission gate, and the two retrieved Wiki pages' actual chunks. This remains a bounded representative check, not a full source-code audit.
unresolved: The Wiki page is a stub and does not establish H81's founder, migration date, full clan history, campaign chronology, or detailed mechanics.

The retrieved Black Orc Wiki chunk confirms only that Black Orcs are native to the Serpentspine; it does not support the 5400 BA Agroloth Confluence migration claim. That date/route is retained as an explicitly unverified prior research attribution pending an exact supporting chunk.

Only representative mission mechanics were checked (the H81 Tag gate, a colonization/institution gate, and a vampire/frenzy gate). Altar/mask/reserve systems, the regional endgame, Karashar formation conditions, and the exact 36-mission count were not exhaustively audited; detailed gameplay claims remain bounded by this source review.

rationale.campaign_length: The 36 direct missions extend from colonization in the Serpentspine to regional conquest and religious unification in Bulwar, making this a long campaign.
rationale.colonization: Early on, you must colonize the Serpentspine caverns and open the way through holds; colonization speed directly affects mission progress.
rationale.complexity: Religious power, altar strength, mask levels and capacity, estates, reserves, and colonization all require concurrent management.
rationale.dark_story: Institutionalized sacrifice, masks made from flayed skin, population reserves, and vampire theocracy place this among the darkest entries in the catalogue.
rationale.difficulty: Military growth is strong, but the layered mechanics, enclosed geography, and event triggers demand careful route planning.
rationale.diplomacy: The country mainly views its neighbors as targets of conquest, sources of sacrifices, and sources of masks; long-term diplomacy is not the core loop.
rationale.early_pressure: The Serpentspine warband start must handle institutions, colonization, expeditions, migration, and nearby wars at once, and waiting can interrupt the pace.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: The blood altar, moonlight, Blood Moon, racial masks, mage privileges, and vampire rituals together form the core system.
rationale.narrative_density: Missions and events tell the cult's rise, its victims' fates, and the adventurers' resistance, with clear phase transitions.
rationale.tall_play: The altar and spoils pile reward investment in the heartland, but the overall objectives continually push the player toward wider expansion.
rationale.trade_economy: Spoils and plunder matter, but there is no independent trade-oriented economic storyline.
rationale.warfare: Conquest, plunder, special wars, and regional wars beyond the Serpentspine run throughout the mission tree.

identity.appearance: A Black Orc Serpentspine warband in 1444; its complete dedicated route remains H81

national_ideas.scope_note: National traditions, seven national ideas, and the ambition; excludes optional idea groups and racial/government bonuses. Alternative sets and their conditions are listed separately and are not assumed to stack; whether a new set is accepted on formation depends on the actual event or decision and player choice.

description.text:
A monster is said to haunt the dark caverns and crumbling halls of the Serpentreach: the Masked Butcher. It has been described as an orc who wears a mask made from the flesh of his victims and paints its skin with their blood. To some, it is but a myth that personifies the horrors of the Dwarovar, but it is all too real to us...

Because we are the Masked Butcher. It is not one beast that hunts these halls but our entire people. There is no limit to what counts as our prey, and in times of war, these eerie tales and our clan's hunting tradition translate well into guerrilla tactics and strike fear into any armies that dare enter our land.

description.text:
When a young orc of the clan reaches maturity, they must face a rite of passage: they are sent off on a hunt, only returning when they have proven themselves. A young orc may go weeks before returning home, returning loaded down with slaughtered prey.

The kills will be stripped of loot and body parts to act as trophies but the greatest of the kills will have its flesh removed and turned into a mask for the newly matured orc. This mask signifies the beginning of an orc's life as a hunter and is worn as a mark of prestige and rank in the clan's hierarchy.

description.text:
For ages, our clan was small and our deeds were merely chalked up as a monster in myth. That was until most orcs began leaving the Serpentreach in droves for the Western Dwarovar. One of our most powerful neighbors left behind its throne and a magnificent altar lit up by natural light from above.

No sign could be clearer that we, the orcs who stayed behind, were destined to rule the Serpentreach. Now, many years have passed since we claimed this throne and we have grown far beyond the small clan we once were. Our population continues to boom and with all the open space and little to no competition, our expansion outward sees no end in sight.

description.text:
A term that roughly translates to "The Count", our clan values what you have killed and the quality of that kill as that is what truly shows strength. On the battlefield, our orcs are savage as all seek to raise their rank in the clan by killing more and slaying the greatest foe. Even better if an orc can take them alive, as a sacrifice in front of all to see makes it undisputed that you killed them.

In every battle, the best rises above the rest. In every battle, the rest try to rise above the best. This way of life makes it to where our troops are always inspired to improve and learn from every fight to do better in the next while our generals are always made up of the greatest among them.

description.text:
All could see me standing in the dim light with my hand placed over the chest of my captive who lay flat on the altar, and yet I couldn’t see anything beyond but the surrounding pitch black and a few stars just barely peeking through from above. Silence, even from those who wished not to be, filled this cavern to the brim. Nothing had ever tested my patience before more than this uneasy excitement for a passing light to say go. The skylight began to shift to a deep red and the moment the Moon slightly emerged I struck with unparalleled strength and tore out the heart of my captive and held it up high towards the light. Two types of screams followed: cheers and cries. As the red moonlight began to pour into the cavern banishing that pitch black darkness, I finally could see the hundreds of orcs in wait rushing forward dragging their captives with them toward the altar. It only lasted about an hour but more blood was spilt in that time than any night before it. Throughout the celebration, I could only think about the nights that have yet to come.

-Chieftain Vrirrig Beardbutcher's account of the first accurately predicted blood moon.

description.text:
The throne and altar are the center of our clan. Thousands live nearby while thousands more flock in to make sacrifices there. Unfortunately, the cave the throne and altar lie in was never meant to support such a vast population and influx of travelers.

To amend this overcrowding, we will undertake a massive excavation and redesign of this cavern. We shall build a central structure that reaches up higher towards the light, with the altar at the very top alongside the Chief's expanded throne room. Around this structure, we shall carve roads and lesser dwellings, to smooth travel and create efficient residences. What started as no more than a bloodied altar will become the beating heart of these mountains.

description.text:
We are Bala-karvash, "Apex Predators". We are hunters in search of the deadliest game. The very top of the food chain. The bravest warriors quickly learn that bravado will not save them from our diligence. The toughest soldiers quickly learn that strength will not save them from our physical superiority. The mightiest beasts quickly learn that instinct will not save them from our tactics.

All quickly learn that they are the ones being hunted. Whether in the bushes or out on the open battlefield, we hold out and wait for the perfect opportunity then pounce when the moment is right.

player_overview.avoid_if: Avoid this country if you dislike waiting for colonization and events, managing complex religion and estates, or playing a state centered on slaughter, flaying, and institutionalized sacrifice.
player_overview.how_it_plays: Colonize the Serpentspine and complete expeditions early; use plunder and sacrifice in the middle game to upgrade the altar, mages, and masks; then establish reserves among different races and leave the mountains, spreading the Blood Moon cult into Bulwar through continuous warfare.
player_overview.overview: The Masked Butcher is a Black Orc horror campaign starting at Bloodied Altar in the Serpentspine. You colonize caverns, expedition into holds, and plunder spoils, then use blood to summon the Blood Moon, carve masks from different peoples, and empower the mage estate. In the middle and late game, the state turns toward vampire theocracy, makes conquered populations into long-term reserves, and pushes beyond the mountains to spread the Night. Its mechanics are dense and its expansion is powerful, but event waits and its extreme brutality will not suit everyone.
player_overview.recommended_for: Recommended for players who enjoy a monster's point of view, dark narratives, relentless conquest, layered resource management, and adaptable builds.
signature_features: The spoils pile continually strengthens the blood altar and connects it to moonlight, the mage estate, missionary activity, and mask capacity.
Accumulate religious power through bloodshed, then allocate it among Blood Rage, summoning the Blood Moon, and carving masks.
Make and upgrade masks according to the victim race, turning conquest targets into distinct build abilities and a continuing reserve for sacrifice.
player_overview.tagline: Make the Serpentspine a Blood Moon altar: feed theocracy with plunder and assemble an evolving monster state from the masks of different peoples.

reasons: Masks change the national build according to the targets of conquest, directly linking expansion to mechanical growth.
The blood altar, Blood Moon, religious power, and mage estate form a layered but coherent resource loop.
The dual perspectives of monster and victim give the evil route a fully developed horror narrative.
The campaign has a strong sense of progression from an underground warband to a cross-regional theocracy of night.
warnings: Early colonization, institutions, and certain mask events may involve long waits.
Resources, estates, masks, and reserves must all be managed at once; complexity is high.
The central narrative explicitly includes slaughter, flaying, blood sacrifice, and keeping populations in reserve.

values.rationale: Massacres, making masks from flayed skin, blood sacrifice, and confining multiple sapient peoples as an ongoing blood supply are embedded in the state system, making this an extreme case of reducing people to resources and denying their personhood.
